punchline: Britain's national cycling team hired a surgeon to teach its riders how to wash their hands.
thirty_sec: In 2003 British cycling was so weak that a bike maker wouldn't even sell to the team. New director Dave Brailsford went looking for 1 percent gains everywhere: better seats, massage gels, the right pillow and mattress for each rider, even a surgeon teaching hand washing to cut colds. By 2008 they won 8 of 14 road and track golds, and in 2012 Wiggins won the Tour. James Clear later noted open questions about the team's medication exemptions.
